source_note: what every ruling in this file was adjudicated FROM (T-0598). Stated once at the top because this domain's rulings all rest on the same record; a ruling resting on something more specific states that on itself and wins.
note: THIS FILE HOLDS NO MERGES AND IT NEVER WILL. A Newberry index entry is a surname over a citation; it carries no forename, no date and no place beyond the locality of the book it points at. A surname-only merge is always a refusal under the rule this domain inherits, so every identification the index seems to offer is refused here — and the refusals are written down, one by one, because the ABSENCE of a merge reads exactly like a pair nobody has looked at, and the next sweep would do this work again. An identification becomes possible only when the work a card points at is opened and says a forename.

passes.what: Volume 1's 2,579 locality cards against the residents, the 1833-1835 civic lists, the 1840 census heads and the structures. 319 leads offered; 0 merges made.

refusals.rule: Refused twice over. 'Beeubion' is the index heading as the photostat's text layer gives it and is not certainly 'Beaubien' at all — the lead rule would not even offer it, at 0.75 similarity against a 0.86 window. And if it were, 'Beeubion' against 'Jean Baptiste Beaubien' would still be a surname against a man, which is always a refusal here.
refusals.note: The three cards are the most tempting in volume 1: a Chicago family whose name this project already carries, cited to Andreas, to Wood 1881 and to the 1839 directory. They are worth following into those books; they are not worth an identification here.

refusals.rule: 'Calhoun' is the index's heading for every Calhoun family it files, and 'John Calhoun' is one man in this project's residents. A surname against a man is a refusal, and six cards under one heading is six families, not six mentions of him.
refusals.note: Two of the six point at Andreas and at Moses and Kirkland for Chicago. That is where the printer of the Chicago Democrat would be named, if he is named; the index does not name him.

refusals.rule: 'Carpenter' heads twelve cards in volume 1 and 'Philo Carpenter' is one 1835 druggist with two buildings in this model. The index gives no forename on any of the twelve, so 'Carpenter' against 'Philo Carpenter' is refused.
refusals.note: Four of the twelve are Chicago cards — Andreas, Moses and Kirkland, the 1839 directory and Wood 1881 — and the 1839 directory is already in this project's sources. Read it there, not here.

refusals.rule: The lead rule joins 'Clark' and 'Clarke' at 0.91 similarity because the photostat drops final letters constantly. Joining them for the purpose of OFFERING a lead is not joining the families: 'Clark' against 'H. B. Clarke' is refused, and so is the reverse.
refusals.note: 1835 Chicago holds both spellings as different households, which is exactly why the similarity window may widen a lead and may never narrow an identity.

refusals.rule: Fifteen cards head 'Adams' in volume 1 and this project holds one 'William Hanford Adams', a name known only from an 1835 poll list. A surname against a man is a refusal; and this man's own record says the poll list is all the evidence there is.
refusals.note: Among the fifteen is a card citing the 1839 Chicago directory, which is the nearest thing to a test this project could run on him.
